about.title: Rancho Santa Margarita Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Rancho Santa Margarita's road network, from Santa Margarita Parkway to Avenida De Las Flores and Alma Aldea, carries a steady flow of commuters and local traffic, and public records show dozens of injury collisions each year in this Orange County community. Thursday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. see a noticeable rise in reported crashes, likely tied to end-of-week commute patterns. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the days right after matter: insurance adjusters move quickly, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness contact information can disappear. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves, but we connect injured Rancho Santa Margarita residents, free of charge, with independent attorneys who understand how to build a claim rooted in local conditions. There's no obligation, and the attorneys in our network only get paid if your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: California's Filing Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney can help make sure paperwork deadlines aren't missed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce What You Recover
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage of fault is assigned to you. Careful documentation of the crash on roads like Santa Margarita Parkway can help protect against an inflated fault percentage.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Work Against You
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement early, before you know the full extent of your injuries. An attorney can handle that communication so nothing you say is used to minimize your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Rancho Santa Margarita?
items.answer: In California, you typically have two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government vehicle or road defect was involved, the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months, so it's worth getting guidance quickly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, which is why documenting the scene matters.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use early statements, made before injuries are fully understood, to reduce the value of your claim.

items.question: Is there a cost to use LawProactive's service?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free connection service, and we are not a law firm. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
